# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Li_2023_RC88_mouse"))$reference`
* Article: [Clin Transl Sci 2023;16(7):1232-1242](https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.13526)
  (open access; supplementary Data S1 holds Tables S1-S4)

RC88 is a humanized IgG1 anti-mesothelin (MSLN) antibody conjugated to
valine-citrulline MMAE (average drug-to-antibody ratio about 4). Li 2023
translates its xenograft efficacy to a human dose in four steps, and this
article reproduces each one:

1. a two-compartment PK model with parallel linear and Michaelis-Menten
   elimination fitted to mouse serum RC88 (`Li_2023_RC88_mouse`);
2. a full target-mediated drug disposition (TMDD) model fitted to cynomolgus
   monkey serum RC88 (`Li_2023_RC88_monkey`), scaled to humans
   (`Li_2023_RC88_human`);
3. three tumor-growth-inhibition (TGI) models -- Simeoni, Jumbe and Hybrid --
   fitted separately to each xenograft study with the mouse PK fixed (eight
   fits; the Jumbe fit to the OVCAR3-MSLN-3# multiple-dose study did not
   converge);
4. the tumor static concentration (TSC) of each TGI fit combined with the
   human PK to give a weekly efficacious dose.

| Model | Species | Study / cell line | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Li_2023_RC88_mouse` | mouse | OVCAR3-MSLN-3# PK, 0.7 and 2.1 mg/kg | Table 2 |
| `Li_2023_RC88_monkey` | cynomolgus monkey | 0.5, 1.5, 5 mg/kg | Table 2 |
| `Li_2023_RC88_human` | human (projection) | scaled from monkey | Table 2 |
| `Li_2023_RC88_simeoni_ovcar3s_mouse_tgi` | mouse | OVCAR3-MSLN-3# single dose (S) | Table S3 |
| `Li_2023_RC88_simeoni_ovcar3m_mouse_tgi` | mouse | OVCAR3-MSLN-3# multiple dose (M) | Table S3 |
| `Li_2023_RC88_simeoni_h292_mouse_tgi` | mouse | H292-MSLN-9C8 | Table S3 |
| `Li_2023_RC88_jumbe_ovcar3s_mouse_tgi` | mouse | OVCAR3-MSLN-3# (S) | Table S2 |
| `Li_2023_RC88_jumbe_h292_mouse_tgi` | mouse | H292-MSLN-9C8 | Table S2 |
| `Li_2023_RC88_hybrid_ovcar3s_mouse_tgi` | mouse | OVCAR3-MSLN-3# (S) | Table S4 |
| `Li_2023_RC88_hybrid_ovcar3m_mouse_tgi` | mouse | OVCAR3-MSLN-3# (M) | Table S4 |
| `Li_2023_RC88_hybrid_h292_mouse_tgi` | mouse | H292-MSLN-9C8 | Table S4 |

# Population

* **Mouse.** Female Balb/c nude mice (4-5 weeks old at purchase) implanted
  subcutaneously with 3 million OVCAR3-MSLN-3# (mesothelin-transfected
  ovarian cancer) or H292-MSLN-9C8 (mesothelin-transfected lung cancer)
  cells, randomised at about 250 mm^3. Dose groups (Table 1): OVCAR3-MSLN-3#
  single dose 0.7 and 2.1 mg/kg (3 per group); OVCAR3-MSLN-3# and
  H292-MSLN-9C8 0.75, 1.5 and 3 mg/kg q1w x 3 (6 per group); vehicle
  controls. Mouse PK used destructive sampling (3 animals per time point)
  alongside the single-dose efficacy study. RC88 does not bind rodent
  mesothelin.
* **Cynomolgus monkey.** 18 animals (half male, half female), single IV doses
  of 0.5, 1.5 and 5 mg/kg (6 per group), sampled to 672 h. RC88 cross-reacts
  with monkey mesothelin.
* **Human.** No human data; parameters projected from the monkey fit.

The `population` element of each model holds the same information, e.g.
`readModelDb("Li_2023_RC88_monkey")()$population`.

# Source trace

All values come from Li 2023 Table 2 (PK) and supplementary Tables S2-S4
(TGI). Every `ini()` line carries the same reference as an in-file comment.

**PK models (Table 2).**

| Parameter | Mouse | Monkey | Human | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lcl` CL (mL/h/kg) | 0.527 | 0.556 | 0.556 | |
| `lq` CLD (mL/h/kg) | 1.31 | 3.519 | 3.519 | |
| `lvc` V1 (mL/kg) | 67.1 | 35.8 (fixed) | 35.8 | |
| `lvp` V2 (mL/kg) | 49.1 | 16.9 | 16.9 | |
| `lkm` Km (ug/mL) | 5.02 | | | |
| `lvmax` Vmax | 1.73 | | | read as ug/h/kg; see Assumptions |
| `lkon` Kon (1/(ug/mL)/h) | | 0.00124 | 0.00124 | |
| `lkoff` Koff (1/h) | | 0.00442 | 0.00442 | unit printed '1/ug/mL*h' |
| `lkdeg` Kout (1/h) | | 0.00496 | 0.00496 | receptor turnover |
| `lkint` Ke (1/h) | | 0.0154 | 0.0154 | complex elimination |
| `lrbase_target` R (ug/mL) | | 36.6 | 109.8 | human = 3 x monkey |
| Structure | Figure 1a | Figure 1c | Figure 1c | Methods 'PK/PD model' |

**TGI models (Tables S2-S4; equations 1-3).** The mouse PK above is fixed
in every TGI model. `psi` is fixed at 20 and `lrbase_tumor` at 250 mm^3
(Methods: tumors staged at about 250 mm^3).

| Model | Parameter | OVCAR3 (S) | OVCAR3 (M) | H292 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Simeoni (Eq 1) | `ltumorExpGrowth` lambda0 (1/h) | 0.00519 | 0.00519 | 0.007 |
| | `ltumorLinGrowth` lambda1 (mm^3/h) | 2.99 | 2.99 | 3.00 |
| | `ldamageTransit` K1 (1/h) | 0.025 | 0.0266 | 0.0150 |
| | `ldrugSlope` K2 (mL/ug/h) | 0.00277 | 0.00256 | 0.00174 |
| Jumbe (Eq 3) | `lkgrow` Kgrow | 0.032 | -- | 0.042 |
| | `ldamageTransit` 1/t (1/h) | 0.107 | -- | 0.027 |
| | `lkmax` Kmax (unitless) | 5.51 | -- | 21.6 |
| | `lkc50` KC50 (ug/mL) | 21.3 | -- | 30.9 |
| Hybrid (Eq 2) | `ltumorLinGrowth` Kgrow (mm^3/h) | 3.99 | 3.99 | 7.17 |
| | `ltumorExpGrowth` KgEx (1/h) | 0.007 | 0.006 | 0.005 |
| | `ltau` t (h) | 36.7 | 36.0 | 146 |
| | `lkmax` Kmax (1/h) | 0.08 | 0.215 | 0.012 |
| | `lkc50` KC50 (ug/mL) | 26.7 | 42.3 | 3.20 |
| | `ltsmax` Emax (mm^3) | 4967 | 4967 | 57365 |

# Mouse PK (Figure 3a, Table S1)

```{r mouse-pk}
mod_mouse <- readModelDb("Li_2023_RC88_mouse")
obs_mouse <- c(0, 0.083, 4, 12, 24, 48, 72, 96, 120, 168, 240)

ev_mouse <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(c(0.7, 2.1)), function(i) {
  dose <- c(0.7, 2.1)[i]
  bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = i, time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1, cmt = "central"),
    data.frame(id = i, time = sort(unique(c(obs_mouse, seq(0, 240, by = 2)))), amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    mutate(treatment = paste(dose, "mg/kg"))
}))
sim_mouse <- rxSolve(mod_mouse, ev_mouse, keep = "treatment") |> as.data.frame()

ggplot(sim_mouse, aes(time, Cc, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Serum RC88 (ug/mL)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Mouse typical-value profiles", caption = "Replicates Figure 3a of Li 2023.")
```

```{r mouse-nca}
nca_input <- function(sim) {
  sim |>
    filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
    select(id, time, Cc, treatment) |>
    distinct(id, time, .keep_all = TRUE)
}
dose_frame <- function(ev) {
  ev |> filter(evid == 1) |> select(id, time, amt, treatment)
}
run_nca <- function(sim, ev, end) {
  conc <- PKNCAconc(nca_input(sim), Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
  dose <- PKNCAdose(dose_frame(ev), amt ~ time | treatment + id, route = "intravascular")
  intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = end, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
  as.data.frame(pk.nca(PKNCAdata(conc, dose, intervals = intervals)))
}
nca_mouse <- run_nca(sim_mouse, ev_mouse, 240)

ref_mouse <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("0.7 mg/kg", "2.1 mg/kg"),
  cmax = c(9.12, 36.5),
  auclast = c(418, 2118)
)
nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  nca_mouse, ref_mouse,
  by = "treatment", units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", auclast = "h*ug/mL"), tolerance_pct = 20
) |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose" = treatment) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Mouse NCA (0-240 h) versus Li 2023 Table S1 (observed). * differs by more than 20%.", digits = 3)
```

Cmax is within 15% of Table S1. AUC at 0.7 mg/kg is about 1.8-fold above the
observed value and AUC at 2.1 mg/kg about 15% above it: the printed typical
values eliminate RC88 more slowly than the observed data, most visibly at the
low dose where the Michaelis-Menten pathway matters most. The Michaelis-Menten
units question behind this is discussed under Assumptions and deviations.

# Monkey PK (Figure 3b, Table S1)

```{r monkey-pk}
mod_monkey <- readModelDb("Li_2023_RC88_monkey")
doses_monkey <- c(0.5, 1.5, 5)
ev_monkey <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(doses_monkey), function(i) {
  bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = i, time = 0, amt = doses_monkey[i], evid = 1, cmt = "central"),
    data.frame(id = i, time = sort(unique(c(0, 0.083, 0.25, 2, 6, seq(0, 672, by = 4)))), amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    mutate(treatment = paste(doses_monkey[i], "mg/kg"))
}))
sim_monkey <- rxSolve(mod_monkey, ev_monkey, keep = "treatment") |> as.data.frame()

ggplot(sim_monkey, aes(time, Cc, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Serum RC88 (ug/mL)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Cynomolgus monkey typical-value profiles", caption = "Replicates Figure 3b of Li 2023.")

nca_monkey <- run_nca(sim_monkey, ev_monkey, 672)
ref_monkey <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("0.5 mg/kg", "1.5 mg/kg", "5 mg/kg"),
  cmax = c(14.7, 42.8, 132),
  auclast = c(332, 1097, 5777)
)
cmp_monkey <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  nca_monkey, ref_monkey,
  by = "treatment", units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", auclast = "h*ug/mL"), tolerance_pct = 20
)
cmp_monkey |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose" = treatment) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Monkey NCA (0-672 h) versus Li 2023 Table S1 (observed means). * differs by more than 20%.", digits = 3)
```

```{r monkey-check}
# The TMDD fit reproduces the observed exposure of all three dose groups:
# the target-mediated pathway saturates with dose, so AUC rises 17-fold for a
# 10-fold dose range in both the data and the model.
monkey_auc <- nca_monkey |> filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |> arrange(treatment)
stopifnot(
  nrow(monkey_auc) == 3,
  all(abs(monkey_auc$PPORRES / ref_monkey$auclast - 1) < 0.15)
)
```

The model also captures the dose non-proportionality: 0.5 to 5 mg/kg is a
10-fold dose step and a 17-fold AUC step, both observed and simulated.

# Human projection and efficacious dose (Table 4)

Li 2023 replaced the mouse PK in the TGI models by the projected human PK and
chose the q1w dose that holds the tumor static. With a linear (Simeoni) kill
term, stasis over a dosing interval needs the average concentration over the
interval to equal the TSC; the paper's Table 4 doses correspond exactly to the
average concentration over the first week after a single dose,
AUC(0-168 h)/168, matching each TSC.

```{r human-dose}
mod_human <- readModelDb("Li_2023_RC88_human")
cavg_week1 <- function(dose) {
  ev <- bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = 1, time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1, cmt = "central"),
    data.frame(id = 1, time = seq(0, 168, by = 0.25), amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central")
  )
  s <- rxSolve(mod_human, ev) |> as.data.frame() |> distinct(time, .keep_all = TRUE)
  sum(diff(s$time) * (head(s$Cc, -1) + tail(s$Cc, -1)) / 2) / 168
}
dose_for_tsc <- function(tsc) {
  uniroot(function(d) cavg_week1(d) - tsc, c(0.1, 10), tol = 1e-5)$root
}

table4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~label,                        ~tsc, ~published_dose,
  "OVCAR3-MSLN-3# median",       1.84, 1.2,
  "OVCAR3-MSLN-3# lower",        1.22, 0.82,
  "OVCAR3-MSLN-3# upper",        2.32, 1.45,
  "H292-MSLN-9C8 median",        2.38, 1.5,
  "H292-MSLN-9C8 lower",         1.31, 0.88,
  "H292-MSLN-9C8 upper",         3.27, 1.96
) |>
  mutate(
    simulated_dose = vapply(tsc, dose_for_tsc, numeric(1)),
    pct_diff = 100 * (simulated_dose / published_dose - 1)
  )

table4 |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Cell line / TSC" = label, "TSC (ug/mL)" = tsc,
    "Table 4 dose (mg/kg q1w)" = published_dose,
    "Simulated dose (mg/kg q1w)" = simulated_dose, "% diff" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Weekly dose whose first-week average concentration equals the TSC, versus Li 2023 Table 4.")

# Deterministic solve against a printed table rounded to 2-3 digits.
stopifnot(all(abs(table4$pct_diff) < 5))
```

```{r human-profile}
ev_h <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = 1, time = 168 * (0:3), amt = 1.2, evid = 1, cmt = "central"),
  data.frame(id = 1, time = seq(0, 672, by = 2), amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central")
)
sim_h <- rxSolve(mod_human, ev_h) |> as.data.frame()
ggplot(sim_h, aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1.84, linetype = 2) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Serum RC88 (ug/mL)",
       title = "Projected human profile, 1.2 mg/kg q1w x 4",
       caption = "Dashed line: OVCAR3-MSLN-3# median TSC (Table 4).")
```

The projected human exposure is strongly target-mediated: baseline
mesothelin (109.8 ug/mL drug-equivalent) far exceeds the concentration
reached at these doses, so the trough at the end of each week is well below
the TSC even though the weekly average matches it.

# Tumor static concentration (Table 3)

Equation 4 gives the TSC for each TGI fit. The Simeoni and Jumbe values do not
depend on tumor size; the Hybrid value does, and is evaluated here at the
250 mm^3 staging volume.

```{r tsc}
tsc_tab <- tibble::tribble(
  ~model,    ~study,           ~published,
  "simeoni", "ovcar3s",        1.84,
  "simeoni", "ovcar3m",        1.95,
  "simeoni", "h292",           3.27,
  "jumbe",   "ovcar3s",        1.22,
  "jumbe",   "h292",           2.38,
  "hybrid",  "ovcar3s",        2.32,
  "hybrid",  "ovcar3m",        1.37,
  "hybrid",  "h292",           1.31
)
tsc_from_model <- function(model, study) {
  ini_df <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(paste0("Li_2023_RC88_", model, "_", study, "_mouse_tgi")))$iniDf
  p <- function(nm) exp(ini_df$est[ini_df$name == nm])
  switch(model,
    simeoni = p("ltumorExpGrowth") / p("ldrugSlope"),
    jumbe = p("lkgrow") * p("lkc50") / (p("ldamageTransit") * p("lkmax") - p("lkgrow")),
    hybrid = {
      e <- 250
      g <- p("ltumorExpGrowth") * (1 - e / p("ltsmax"))
      sw <- (1 + (p("ltumorExpGrowth") / p("ltumorLinGrowth") * e)^20)^(1 / 20)
      g * p("lkc50") / (p("lkmax") * sw - g)
    }
  )
}
tsc_tab <- tsc_tab |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(computed = tsc_from_model(model, study)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (computed / published - 1))

tsc_tab |>
  dplyr::rename("Model" = model, "Study" = study, "Table 3 TSC (ug/mL)" = published,
                "TSC from Tables S2-S4 (ug/mL)" = computed, "% diff" = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

# The Jumbe TSC formula pins the reading of the Table S2 transit constant:
# multiplying Kkill by 0.107 returns the published 1.22 ug/mL, dividing by it
# would give 0.013 ug/mL.
jumbe_rows <- tsc_tab |> filter(model == "jumbe")
stopifnot(nrow(jumbe_rows) == 2, all(abs(jumbe_rows$pct_diff) < 2))
```

The Jumbe values reproduce Table 3. The Simeoni OVCAR3 values agree within
4%. The others are limited by how the tables are rounded. Table S3 prints
lambda0 for H292 to one significant figure (0.007), and the Hybrid TSC
denominator, Kmax - KgEx(1 - E/Emax), is a small difference of two rounded
numbers (KgEx is printed to one significant figure). Neither can be closer
than these roundings allow. Table 3 also reports the TSCs from the fitting
software's secondary-parameter output rather than from the rounded tables.

# Tumor growth inhibition (Figure 2)

Each TGI model is solved at the doses of its study, starting from the mean
initial tumor volume read from Figure 2 by the maintainers (about 340, 270 and
290 mm^3 for panels a, b and c). The points are the group means read from
Figure 2.

```{r tgi-sim}
solve_tgi <- function(stem, doses, n_doses, v0, tmax) {
  mod <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb(paste0("Li_2023_RC88_", stem, "_mouse_tgi"))) |>
    ini(lrbase_tumor = log(v0))
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(doses), function(i) {
    dose <- doses[i]
    obs <- data.frame(id = i, time = seq(0, tmax, by = 4), amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central")
    ev <- if (dose > 0) {
      bind_rows(data.frame(id = i, time = 168 * (seq_len(n_doses) - 1), amt = dose, evid = 1, cmt = "central"), obs)
    } else {
      obs
    }
    rxSolve(mod, ev) |>
      as.data.frame() |>
      mutate(dose = if (dose > 0) paste(dose, "mg/kg") else "Control")
  })) |>
    mutate(model = sub("_.*", "", stem), study = sub(".*_", "", stem))
}

sim_a <- bind_rows(lapply(c("simeoni_ovcar3s", "jumbe_ovcar3s", "hybrid_ovcar3s"),
                          solve_tgi, doses = c(0, 0.7, 2.1), n_doses = 1, v0 = 340, tmax = 264))
sim_b <- bind_rows(lapply(c("simeoni_ovcar3m", "hybrid_ovcar3m"),
                          solve_tgi, doses = c(0, 0.75, 1.5, 3), n_doses = 3, v0 = 270, tmax = 504))
sim_c <- bind_rows(lapply(c("simeoni_h292", "jumbe_h292", "hybrid_h292"),
                          solve_tgi, doses = c(0, 0.75, 1.5, 3), n_doses = 3, v0 = 290, tmax = 504))

# Group means read from Li 2023 Figure 2 by the maintainers.
fig2 <- bind_rows(

    "Control",   48,  470, "Control",  96,  580, "Control",  168, 715, "Control",  264, 880,
    "0.7 mg/kg", 48,  470, "0.7 mg/kg", 96, 450, "0.7 mg/kg", 168, 390, "0.7 mg/kg", 264, 405,
    "2.1 mg/kg", 48,  405, "2.1 mg/kg", 96, 300, "2.1 mg/kg", 168, 110, "2.1 mg/kg", 264, 60
  ) |> mutate(panel = "a"),
  tibble::tribble(
    ~dose,        ~time, ~tumor_vol,
    "Control",    72, 440, "Control",    168, 760, "Control",    240, 920,
    "Control",    336, 1020, "Control",  408, 1270, "Control",   504, 1660,
    "0.75 mg/kg", 72, 390, "0.75 mg/kg", 168, 340, "0.75 mg/kg", 240, 410,
    "0.75 mg/kg", 336, 560, "0.75 mg/kg", 408, 850, "0.75 mg/kg", 504, 1170,
    "1.5 mg/kg",  72, 300, "1.5 mg/kg",  168, 120, "1.5 mg/kg",  240, 80,
    "1.5 mg/kg",  336, 20, "1.5 mg/kg",  408, 5, "1.5 mg/kg",    504, 5,
    "3 mg/kg",    72, 240, "3 mg/kg",    168, 30, "3 mg/kg",     240, 5,

plot_panel <- function(sim, p, title) {
  ggplot(sim, aes(time, tumor_vol, colour = dose)) +
    geom_line(aes(linetype = model)) +
    geom_point(data = filter(fig2, panel == p), aes(time, tumor_vol, colour = dose), inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Tumor volume (mm^3)", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL, title = title)
}
```

```{r fig2a}
plot_panel(sim_a, "a", "OVCAR3-MSLN-3#, single dose") +

```

```{r tgi-check}
# Structural checks that hold whatever the PK reading: every control arm
# grows, and every model ranks its dose arms in order at the end of the study.
end_vol <- bind_rows(sim_a, sim_b, sim_c) |>
  group_by(model, study, dose) |>
  filter(time == max(time)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(dose_num = ifelse(dose == "Control", 0, as.numeric(sub(" mg/kg", "", dose))))
# 3 models x 3 arms (panel a) + 2 models x 4 arms (b) + 3 models x 4 arms (c)
stopifnot(nrow(end_vol) == 29)
v0_by_study <- c(ovcar3s = 340, ovcar3m = 270, h292 = 290)
ranked <- end_vol |>
  group_by(model, study) |>
  arrange(dose_num, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  summarise(
    control_grows = tumor_vol[dose_num == 0] > 2 * v0_by_study[[study[1]]],
    monotone = all(diff(tumor_vol) <= 1e-6 * max(tumor_vol)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
stopifnot(nrow(ranked) == 8, all(ranked$control_grows), all(ranked$monotone))
```

Every model reproduces the single-dose OVCAR3-MSLN-3# study (panel a), the
regressions at 1.5 and 3 mg/kg in the multiple-dose OVCAR3-MSLN-3# study
(panel b), and the 3 mg/kg H292-MSLN-9C8 arm (panel c). The control arms are
reproduced except the Simeoni H292-MSLN-9C8 fit, which reaches about
1800 mm^3 at 504 h against an observed 2650 mm^3. The fits differ from
Figure 2 at the partially effective doses: 0.75 mg/kg in panel b, and 0.75
and 1.5 mg/kg in panel c. There the models predict more tumor shrinkage than
was observed. Two things limit agreement at those doses. These are
typical-value models with no interindividual variability (Figure 2 shows
group means). The low-dose mouse exposure also depends on the
Michaelis-Menten units question described below.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Mouse Vmax units.** Table 2 labels the mouse Vmax "ug/mL/h". Read as a
  concentration rate (amount rate Vmax x V1), the Michaelis-Menten pathway
  alone removes RC88 with a 2-h half-life at low concentrations. Serum RC88
  after 0.7 mg/kg then falls to about 0.06 ug/mL at 24 h. Figure 3a shows
  about 5 ug/mL at 24 h, with RC88 still measurable at 240 h. That reading
  also gives AUCs about 7-fold below Table S1, and loses the 2.1 mg/kg
  regression in Figure 2a.
  Vmax is therefore encoded as an amount rate per kg body weight (ug/h/kg),
  dimensionally consistent with the per-kg doses and volumes. Under this
  reading Cmax matches Table S1 and AUC is 15% (2.1 mg/kg) to 80% (0.7 mg/kg)
  above it, so the true low-concentration elimination lies between the two
  readings. No scale factor was fitted.
* **Variability.** The paper reports no interindividual or residual
  variability for any fit (Phoenix NLME, FOCE-ELS). Every model therefore
  carries a single `fixed(0)` proportional residual error and no etas; it
  simulates the typical value only.
* **Simeoni growth term.** Equation 1 uses E1 (cycling cells) in both the
  numerator and the exponential-to-linear switch. The original Simeoni 2004
  model uses total tumor weight in the switch. The printed equation is
  encoded.
* **Jumbe transit constant.** Table S2 calls `t` a "transit rate constant"
  with unit "(h)", and Equation 3 prints 1/t. The tabulated value is used
  wherever Equation 3 prints 1/t, because only this reading makes the
  paper's TSC formula return its Table 3 TSCs (1.22 and 2.38 ug/mL). The
  Jumbe growth constant Kgrow is labelled 1/h but multiplies volume^(2/3), as
  printed.
* **Jumbe non-negativity.** A rate proportional to volume^(2/3) can empty a
  compartment in finite time. Each volume^(2/3) term is evaluated on
  `max(state, 0)` so an emptied compartment stays at zero, where the
  equations are undefined below zero.
* **Initial tumor volume.** The paper used each animal's measured volume as
  the E1 initial condition. The models default to the 250 mm^3 staging
  volume; this article overrides it with the Figure 2 group means.
* **H292 PK.** The mouse PK was measured in OVCAR3-MSLN-3# tumor-bearing
  mice. The paper fixed the same PK for the H292-MSLN-9C8 fits, and the
  models do the same.
* **Text discrepancies.** The Results text gives the top monkey dose as
  3 mg/kg; Methods, Figure 3b and Table S1 all give 5 mg/kg, which is used
  here. Table 1 lists 3 animals per group for the single-dose OVCAR3 study;
  the Methods text says 6. Table S3 prints identical lambda0 and RSE for the
  OVCAR3 (S) and (M) Simeoni fits.
* **Human projection.** All human parameters are fixed scaled values
  (allometric exponent 1 on the per-kg clearances and volumes, rate
  constants 1:1, baseline mesothelin x3 for disease). They are not
  estimates from human data.
